entry.title: EMF Campus AI in Banking Presentation

link.title: EMF Campus AI in Banking Presentation

entry.content:
I held a presentation at SDA Bocconi on the 20th of June 2024. The event, EMF CampUS, was a forum for discussion among EMF Alumni focused on lifelong learning and continuous improvement. My presentation was part of the Banking track and entitled Banking Transformation with AI: Optimizing Processes, Enhancing Productivity, and Real-World Applications.

You can find more details in the LinkedIn post here.

entry.title: Crunch Dao Community Presentation
entry.content:
I was invited to hold a presentation to the Crunch Dao Community. The talk entitled Machine Learning Algorthms in Financial Markets focused on explaining how to create an intraday trading strategy using machine learning approaches taken from the most recent academic literature.

entry.title: AAAI 2024 conference Bridge
entry.content:
I was invited to hold a seminar at the AAAI 2024 conference Bridge - AI for Financial Services, on the topic of Machine Learning in Financial Markets. This seminar was held together with Matteo Rampazzo, a colleague from Epsilon SGR. We started with a brief introduction on the uses of algorithms in the financial markets followed by an overview of the tecnical machine learning tools. We then had three main sections, the first on quantitative trading, then quantitative investing and finally on optimal execution.

Download the slides [PDF]

entry.title: New Space Economy - Expoforum Rome 2023
entry.content:
I had the honor of contributing to the “Moon Opportunities” round table at the NSE ExpoForum and present a study on the economic feasibility of Moon mining and in-orbit refuelling, based on a research developed with SDA Bocconi’s Space Economy Evolution Lab. entry.title: ICAIF 2023 conference - New York
entry.content:
This year, with colleagues from Intesa Sanpaolo, we submitted a paper which was accepted to the fourth edition of the International Conference on AI in Finance, 27 November - 29 December 2023 (website). The paper is: CVA Hedging with Reinforcement Learning. It was awarded the Runner-up Best Industrial Paper Award!

entry.title: RL for Algorithmic Trading - King’s College

link.title: RL for Algorithmic Trading - King’s College

entry.content:
I gave my first 2 hour lecture to the students of the MSc in Computational Finance at King’s College London. The topic was Reinforcement Learning in the Capital Markets. I had the chance to present most of my research, explaining how RL can be used to solve problems in the trading and hedging space.

Download the full slides [PDF].

entry.title: EMFCampus 2022 seminar - SDA Bocconi
entry.content:
On November 11 2022, together with the Cristian Giacomini, the CEO of Modefinance International and Emilio Colombo from Cerved, I held a seminar on Machine Learning Applications in Finance: Credit Scoring, Real Estate and Algorithmic Trading. I started with an introduction to machine learning and then explained two use cases of Algo Trading with RL.

entry.title: Ph.D. Dissertation Defense - Politecnico di Milano

link.title: Ph.D. Dissertation Defense - Politecnico di Milano

entry.content:
I obtained the Ph.D. with a thesis entitled Augmenting Traders with Learning Machines.
The thesis can be found at this link, while the slides used for the defense can be found here.

Abstract

The financial markets are comprised of several participants with diverse roles and objectives. Asset management firms optimize the portfolios of pension funds, institutions and private individuals; market makers offer liquidity by continuously pricing and hedging their risks; proprietary traders invest their own capital with sophisticated methodologies. The approaches adopted by these actors are either manual or expert systems that rely on the experience of traders, and thus are subject to human bias and error.

This dissertation proposes innovative techniques to address the limitations of the current trading strategies. Specifically, we explore the use of algorithms capable of autonomously learning the aforementioned sequential decision-making processes. The development of these algorithms entails a careful reproduction of realistic environments, as well as the observance of trading objectives, i.e., maximizing returns while maintaining a low risk profile and minimizing costs. These algorithms all share a common core structure, that is making a trading decision conditional on the current state of the financial markets.

Our main theoretical and algorithmic contributions include the extension of the online learning field, as we introduce transaction costs and conservativeness in online portfolio optimization, and the enhancement of Monte Carlo Tree Search algorithms to account for the stochasticity and high noise typical of the financial markets. In terms of experimental contributions, we apply Reinforcement Learning to learn profitable quantitative trading strategies and option hedging approaches superior to the standard Black & Scholes hedge. We also find that Reinforcement Learning combined with Mean Field Games enables the development of competitive bond market making strategies. Finally, we demonstrate that dynamic optimal execution methods can be learned through Thompson Sampling with Reinforcement Learning.

The use of such advanced techniques in a production environment may allow the achievement of a competitive advantage that will translate into economical benefits.
